newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia's ousted PM Ranariddh to visit King.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's ousted PM Ranariddh to visit King.

text.p: Cambodia's ousted first prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh is to pay a private visit to his father, King Norodom Sihanouk, in Beijing, the king said in a statement on Thursday.
"This visit has no political nature," Sihanouk said in a statement issued from his residence in Beijing, where he has been undergoing medical treatment for several months.
"My son... wishes simply to see me after a separation of several months," said Sihanouk, who reigns but does not rule in Cambodia.
He gave no date for the visit, but said it would take place "very soon".

Ranariddh visited Jakarta on Wednesday for a closed-door meeting with President Suharto, while in Kuala Lumpur the government of his rival co-Prime Minister Hun Sen, who overthrew him in a coup this month, asked for mediation by the Association of South East Asian Nations.
ASEAN has postponed Cambodia's entry into the group, originally scheduled for this week, because of the political crisis.
Sihanouk said that, as a constitutional monarch, he took no sides in the dispute between the two prime ministers.
However, he urged all sides to follow Cambodia's constitution as well as the 1991 Paris peace accords that ended decades of bloodshed in his homeland.
Jakarta was co-chair of the 1991 Paris talks, which laid the ground for United Nations-sponsored elections in 1993.
Ranariddh won the poll and agreed to an uneasy power-sharing coalition with Hun Sen as second prime minister, a relationship that began to unravel months before Ranariddh's ouster.
ASEAN held a special ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday to welcome new members Burma and Laos. Other members are Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Ranariddh was due in Bangkok on Thursday where he would meet U.S. President Bill Clinton's special envoy, former congressman Stephen Solarz.
